He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==Early life== Born in Fairfax, Virginia to mother, Tammy Hill, Dawkins was raised by Andre and Pamela Dawkins. He started his high school basketball career at [[Deep Creek High School]] in [[Chesapeake, Virginia]], before transferring to Atlantic Shores Christian School, where he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] as a freshman. He was a three-time first team all-state, all-conference, and all-state tournament team selection. He was named conference player of the year as a sophomore, after averaging 22.4 points and 7.0 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204812451 |title=Andre Dawkins Bio – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=September 19, 1991 |access-date=March 31, 2010}} ==College career== In June 2008, Dawkins committed to join [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] in 2010, but in July 2009 he announced he would graduate a year ahead of schedule to enroll at [[Duke University]] in time for the [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2009–10 season]], following the transfer of guard, [[Elliot Williams]], to [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].{{cite news|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/college-basketball/article/2009-07-16/andre-dawkins-accelerates-graduation-will-step-for-elliot-will|title=Andre Dawkins accelerates graduation, will step in for Elliot Williams at Duke|first=Mike|last=DeCourcy|date=July 16, 2009|work=[[Sporting News]]|access-date=March 14, 2010|archive-date=January 7, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100107030951/http://www.sportingnews.com/college-basketball/article/2009-07-16/andre-dawkins-accelerates-graduation-will-step-for-elliot-will|url-status=dead}} In December 2009 an automobile accident in [[West Virginia]] killed Dawkins' sister, Lacey, and injured their mother, Tamara Hill. The two had been on their way from [[Columbus, Ohio]], to see Dawkins play against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]].{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldsun.com/pages/full_story/push?article-Dawkins-+sister+killed+in++car+crash%20&id=5031838-Dawkins-+sister+killed+in++car+crash&instance=main_article|work=[[The Herald-Sun (Durham, North Carolina)|The Herald-Sun]]|title=Sister of Duke's Dawkins killed in car crash|date=December 7, 2009|first=Bryan|last=Strickland|access-date=March 14, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725215647/http://www.heraldsun.com/pages/full_story/push?article-Dawkins-+sister+killed+in++car+crash%20&id=5031838-Dawkins-+sister+killed+in++car+crash&instance=main_article|archive-date=July 25, 2011|url-status=dead}} He played in 38 games in the 2009–10 season, averaging 12.6 minutes and 4.4 points per game.{{cite web|url=http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/statlines.php?playerid=2737 |title=The Official On-Line Home Of Duke Statistics |publisher=GoDuke.StatsGeek.com |access-date=April 6, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100405021406/http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/statlines.php?playerid=2737| archive-date= April 5, 2010 | url-status= live}} As a freshman, he was a back-up guard on Duke's 2010 [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|national champion]] team. In the NCAA tournament [[Elite Eight]] game (March 28, 2010) against Baylor, Dawkins hit two crucial three-pointers in the first half to help Duke stay in the game. In the Summer of 2012, Duke announced that Dawkins would redshirt the 2012–13 season.{{cite news| last =Eisenberg | first =Jeff | title =It's official: Duke's Andre Dawkins will redshirt next season | work =Yahoo Sports| date =June 21, 2012 | url =https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger-college-basketball-blog/official-duke-andre-dawkins-redshirt-next-season-205741819--ncaab.html | access-date = September 3, 2012}} On April 11, 2013, Dawkins announced he was returning to Duke for his Senior season and changing his number from 20 to 34 (a nod to one of his idols, [[Ray Allen]], who changed his number from 20 to 34 for the final stage of his career when he joined the [[Miami Heat]]).[https://twitter.com/dre_dawkins/status/322454458082684928 I have changed my number to 34...] ==Professional career== ===2014–15 season=== After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Dawkins joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].[http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-announce-summer-league-information-0 HEAT Announce Summer League Information] On September 23, 2014, he signed with the Heat.[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-andre-dawkins-and-shawn-jones HEAT Signs Shawn Jones and Andre Dawkins] On December 3, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]].[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-assign-andre-dawkins-skyforce HEAT Assign Andre Dawkins to Skyforce] On December 21, he was recalled by the Heat.[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-recall-andre-dawkins-skyforce HEAT Recall Andre Dawkins From Skyforce] On January 6, 2015, he was waived by the Heat after appearing in just four games.[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-andre-dawkins HEAT Waive Andre Dawkins] Six days later, he was acquired by the Skyforce.{{Cite web |url=http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/sxf-acquires-dawkins/ |title=Sioux Falls Acquires Guard Andre Dawkins |access-date=January 13, 2015 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304042137/http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/sxf-acquires-dawkins/ |url-status=dead }} On January 23, 2015, Dawkins signed a 10-day contract with the [[Boston Celtics]], but was immediately assigned to their D-League affiliate, the [[Maine Red Claws]].[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-sign-andre-dawkins-10-day-contract Celtics Sign Andre Dawkins to 10-Day Contract] He was recalled on the afternoon of January 29, but was reassigned to Maine later that day after one practice with the Celtics.[http://www.masslive.com/celtics/index.ssf/2015/01/andre_dawkins_recalled_from_ma.html Andre Dawkins reassigned to Maine Red Claws after one practice with Boston Celtics] On February 1, he was recalled again by the Celtics to suit up for their home game against his former team, the Miami Heat.[http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasybasketball/update/25015158/celtics-recall-james-young-andre-dawkins-from-nbadl Celtics recall James Young, Andre Dawkins from NBADL] The next day, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Celtics.[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/misc-020215-celtics-sign-andre-dawkins-second-10-day-contract Celtics Sign Andre Dawkins to Second 10-Day Contract] On February 5, he was reassigned to Maine,[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-assign-andre-dawkins-and-phil-pressey-maine-red-claws Boston Celtics Assign Andre Dawkins and Phil Pressey to Maine Red Claws] only to be recalled again five days later.[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-recall-andre-dawkins-maine-red-claws Boston Celtics Recall Andre Dawkins from Maine Red Claws] Following the expiration of his second 10-day contract on February 12, he parted ways with the Celtics before appearing in a game for them. Two days later, he returned to the Sioux Falls Skyforce.[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4927285 Skyforce Acquire Mullens and Re-Acquire Dawkins] ===2015–16 season=== On August 13, 2015, Dawkins signed with [[Auxilium CUS Torino]] of Italy for the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Andre Dawkins inks with Auxilium CUS Torino|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/172607/andre-dawkins-inks-with-auxilium-cus-torino.html|access-date=August 13, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 13, 2015}} On March 8, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite news|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |title=NBA D-League Transactions |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 9, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309163514/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=March 9, 2016 }} That night, he made his debut with the Legends in a 111–93 loss to the [[Idaho Stampede]], recording 14 points and three rebounds in 22 minutes off the bench.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160308/IDATEX/|title=Stampede Run Past Legends|work=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2016|access-date=March 9, 2016|archive-date=January 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118030109/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160308/IDATEX/|url-status=dead}} ===2016–17 season=== After appearing in five games for the Legends and averaging 11.5 points and four rebounds per game, Dawkins was traded to the [[Windy City Bulls]] on December 1, 2016, for the returning player rights of [[Xavier Thames]].{{cite web|url=http://windycity.dleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-acquire-andre-dawkins/|title=Windy City Bulls Acquire Andre Dawkins|work=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2016|access-date=December 4, 2016|archive-date=December 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221033907/http://windycity.dleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-acquire-andre-dawkins/|url-status=dead}} On January 28, 2017, he was traded back to the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|url=http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-complete-trade-windy-city/|title=Legends Complete Trade With Windy City|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2017|access-date=January 30, 2017|archive-date=February 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203155312/http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-complete-trade-windy-city/|url-status=dead}} ===2017–18 season=== On August 23, 2017, Dawkins was
